rationale: The two-case control executed and was retained (CheckRun beca431464bf44ab9c3354145c21899f, exit 0, tests_passed). Running the identical legal five-node history twice, differing only in how much log the successor keeps when it snapshots inside the follower's stale suffix, separates cause from symptom: with TrailingLogs=0 the follower installs the same snapshot ~697 times and never advances, while with TrailingLogs=3 the very same history converges with zero snapshot installs. This update records the measured interpretation and promotes the paired operands to a Fact.

knowledge.statement: Paired execution in one receipt: the TrailingLogs=0 case produced divergent_prefix {base_index 2, divergence_index 3, partitioned_leader_last_index 7, partner_last_index 7, partner_store 1..7}, successor_snapshot {snapshot_index 4, successor_store_first/last 0}, a timeline of partner InstallSnapshot installs 102, 214, 332, 452, 568, 687 at 0..1300 ms with partner_applied_cmds staying 1, and rejoin_observe {restores_before 0, restores_early 687, restores_late 697, partner_applied_index 4, partner_last_index 7, partner_store 5..7}. The TrailingLogs=3 case produced the same precondition and the same snapshot index {snapshot_index 4, successor_store_first 2, successor_store_last 4}, a timeline of partner installs flat at 0 for the whole window, and rejoin_observe {restores_before/early/late 0, partner_applied_index 4, partner_last_index 4, partner_store 1..4}.
knowledge.conditions: One process, root package '.', MakeClusterCustom with five bootstrapped nodes over InmemTransport/InmemStore, both cases sharing every setting except TrailingLogs (0 versus 3); the fault is a two-sided partition of {leader, partner} from the other three peers, healed with FullyConnect after the successor snapshotted inside the partner's stale suffix. Frozen snapshot fd2d6988362c434e9fda87b87c5fb0df.

interpretations.rationale: The predicate under test was that the outcome of this legal history does not depend on how much log the leader retains once it snapshots inside the follower's stale suffix: on that reading both cases should either converge or both should fail. Retained receipt CheckRun beca431464bf44ab9c3354145c21899f contradicts it, so the comparison is violated. The two cases share the partition, the uncommitted suffix, the snapshot index (4) and the observation window; the only difference is compaction depth. TrailingLogs=0: index 1 shows the precondition (partner_store 1..7, divergence_index 3), index 2 shows the successor's store fully compacted (first/last 0), and index 9 shows 687 to 697 InstallSnapshot installs with the partner's applied index pinned at 4 and its advertised last index stuck at 7. TrailingLogs=3: index 11 shows the same precondition, index 12 shows the successor retaining 2..4, and index 19 shows restores_before/early/late all 0 with the partner's applied and last index both at 4. Mechanism, matching the source: with the retained log starting above the index needed to rebuild the request, the leader's rewind to the snapshot boundary produces ErrLogNotFound, replicateTo branches to SEND_SNAP, and the re-installed snapshot restores nextIndex to the boundary again, so the same rejection recurs and the follower never advances; retaining even a few entries below the boundary lets the leader walk the prev-log index down into entries it still holds, the follower's conflicting suffix is truncated by ordinary AppendEntries, and no snapshot is transferred. Scoped defect claim: in hashicorp/raft fd2d6988362c434e9fda87b87c5fb0df, once a leader has compacted its log past the boundary a rejoining follower needs, that follower cannot be repaired - it repeatedly receives the whole snapshot while its applied index stays at the snapshot index - and this is a bounded-liveness failure for that follower under the stated conditions, with no enabled repair in the observed interval. This control also answers the outstanding reachability and cause gaps: the precondition is reached by real producers, and the failure requires compaction past the boundary rather than the partition or the snapshot alone.
counterevidence: With TrailingLogs=3 the identical history converges with zero snapshot installs, so compaction depth is load-bearing and the failure is not a property of the partition, the uncommitted suffix or the snapshot transfer by itself.
The follower's applied index and last index are pinned for the observed ~1.5 s; the claim is bounded to that interval plus the source-traced retry cycle, not a proof of infinite stalling.
limitations: Both cases used in-process InmemTransport/InmemStore and FileSnapshotStore, with equal 1 s timeouts; no network transport and no other timeout regime was sampled.
The default TrailingLogs (10240) was not sampled: it should delay the condition (the leader must extend that far past its snapshot index) rather than remove it, but that was not executed.
The exact retention threshold between 0 and 3 was not characterised, and the transfers are counted through the follower FSM's Restore count rather than on the wire.
One snapshot index and one five-node configuration; the number of installs (~700 per 1.5 s) is a property of this harness, not a production rate.
interpretations.joint_history: Single receipt, both cases: indices 1/2/9 (TrailingLogs=0) and 11/12/19 (TrailingLogs=3) come from one execution of the registered two-case experiment on the same frozen snapshot; each case is a separate cluster built by the same harness, and the events carry trailing_logs so the cases are not conflated.
